title: Finite Tor amplitude of a module model on an affine open
statement: Let S be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], U an affine open and R = Gamma(U,O_S). Let K in D(O_S) [def-pc-derived-category] have finite Tor dimension [def-pc-finite-tor-dimension]. Let P be any complex of R-modules whose image under the explicit affine sheafification functor F_U [lem-pc-affine-perfect-module-model] represents the restriction of K to the localized site over U. Then there exist integers a <= b such that Q(P) has Tor amplitude in [a,b] over R: for every R-module N, H^i(Q(P) tensor_R^L N) = 0 for i outside [a,b]. No pseudo-coherence or boundedness of P is assumed.

source.place: Tag 08E9(1), combined with Cohomology of Sheaves Tag 08CG and Derived Categories of Schemes Tag 08DX(2)

proof.text: Choose the global interval a <= b from [def-pc-finite-tor-dimension]. For every module sheaf G on U, test with its direct image along the open inclusion. Restriction of this direct image is G, and exact restriction commutes with derived tensor by [lem-pc-derived-tensor-open-restriction-universes]. Hence the same bounds hold for K restricted to U.

Use isoSpec and the localized-site equivalence in [lem-pc-affine-localized-site-derived-transport] to transport to Spec R. These exact equivalences preserve the structure sheaf, tensor and cohomology. The representing isomorphism identifies the resulting object with Q(tilde P).

Apply [lem-pc-affine-tor-amplitude-criterion] from sheaf Tor amplitude to module Tor amplitude, keeping a <= b as the witnesses. Empty affine opens, zero rings and unbounded representatives are included.

proof_origin.place: Tag 08E9(1); locality as in Tags 08CG and 08DX
